Waveform

The Waveform control displays peak amplitudes supplied by your application. It can also highlight how far playback has progressed through the data.

Properties and Methods

  • WaveformData: The float[] containing the peaks. Negative values are displayed using their magnitude, and nonfinite samples are ignored.
  • ScaleAmmount: Scales the displayed amplitude. Note that the current property name is spelled ScaleAmmount.
  • ProgressValue: The playback position as a value between 0 and 1. Completed cells use FocusedForeground.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

MXML Example

App refers to the SettingsModel backend from the Data Binding Guide. Register it with page.BackendObjects.Add("App", model) before compiling.

Output Example

Notes

Waveform only draws data. It does not decode music files, play audio, or manage audio devices.

App.Peaks in the MXML example is a public float[] property. Bind an array from your backend; a comma-separated string does not create a float array.

The data is resampled to fit the available width. The output example does not show the progress color because it is a plain text capture.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
